summary.intent: Extract shared-folder write operations from the React web UI (useSharedNavigation hook) into stateless SDK functions, add test coverage, and refactor the web UI to use the SDK as thin wrappers.
summary.outcome: A GSD quick task (260327-2ab) was planned and executed to create sdk/src/share/shared-write.ts with 6 stateless write functions plus SDK/sdk-core unit tests and web UI refactor. The executor was spawned but transcript ends before confirming completion.

repo: The SDK currently only covers the owner's perspective for share operations (shareFolder, revokeShare, reWrapForRecipients); the recipient write path was entirely missing from the SDK as of phase 27.
The SDK's ShareCallbacks type uses 'file' | 'folder' key types but the web UI has expanded this to 'file-ipns' | 'folder-ipns' — the SDK types need widening.
updateFolderMetadataAndPublish exists in sdk-core for the owner side; publishSharedFolderMetadata in the web UI is the recipient-side counterpart using re-wrapped IPNS keys.
uint8ToBase64 is already a utility in sdk-core — web UI has a duplicate that should be removed.
The web UI uses a withRevocationGuard/isForbiddenError pattern to detect 403 responses and transition to read-only; any SDK consumer doing shared writes needs this same pattern.

code.finding: publishSharedFolderMetadata — recipient-side equivalent of sdk-core's updateFolderMetadataAndPublish; encrypts folder metadata, uploads to IPFS, publishes IPNS using re-wrapped key.
withRevocationGuard — wraps write operations to detect 403 and transition shared folder to read-only; needed as SDK utility.
isForbiddenError — helper used by withRevocationGuard to classify 403 responses.
refreshFolderContents — resolves IPNS, decrypts shared folder metadata, returns children + sequence number; variant of sdk-core's fetchAndDecryptMetadata tailored for shared-folder context.
updateSharePermission — calls sharesControllerUpdatePermission; natural addition to SDK share module alongside createShare/revokeShare.
Fire-and-forget reWrapForRecipients call after file update — SDK's write path should bake in this 'after any mutation, re-wrap for recipients' pattern.

workflow: The GSD quick workflow init produces a JSON with planner/executor/checker/verifier model assignments, quick_id (YYMMDD-xxx format), slug, and directory paths used throughout orchestration.
Quick tasks update STATE.md 'Quick Tasks Completed' table but do NOT touch ROADMAP.md — intentional separation from planned phase tracking.
The analysis-then-implement pattern (first session analyzed candidacy, second session executed extraction) worked well for a task of this scope.
